# Accounts banned for NOISE — off-topic, spammy, or disruptive traffic aimed at this project.
#
# This is NOT the eval-gaming denylist. Compare the two before adding anyone:
#
#   .github/blocked-contributors.txt  sybil / emission farming. PERMANENT. The PR is labeled
#                                     `flagged:gaming`, commented, CLOSED, and never evaluated.
#   .github/noise-ban-list.txt (here) noise. TEMPORARY (3 days). Nothing is closed and no
#                                     measurement is thrown away — the account's eval tiers are
#                                     parked so they earn nothing for the window, then restored.
#
# The penalty (eval/noise_penalty.py, run hourly by .github/workflows/noise-penalty.yml):
# every `eval*:<tier>` label on the account's PRs is swapped for `eval*:<tier>-p` for 3 days.
# SN74 scoring reads `eval:*`, so a parked tier scores nothing. The tier stays spelled out in the
# label, so when the ban lifts the bot puts back exactly what the eval measured — a ban costs the
# account 3 days of emissions, never a verdict it actually earned.
#
# `eval:none` is exempt in every family: it is worth nothing already, and it is the marker the
# bots use to record "evaluated, no speedup". Parking it would only lose that record.
#
# TWO LEVELS. A first offence is always `warn` — on the record, nothing parked. That is the one
# life CONTRIBUTING.md promises, and it is what makes a later `ban` fair rather than a surprise.
# Only a repeat is written as `ban`.
#
# Format — one account per line:
#
#   <github-login>  <YYYY-MM-DD start, UTC>  <warn|ban>   # why
#
# The level defaults to `warn` when it is left off, so a half-written line can never penalise
# anyone. The date is the START and never changes; a ban lifts at start + 3 days. Escalating or
# re-offending means editing that account's line, not adding a second one.
#
# Leave expired entries in place — they are the record of what was done and to whom. An expired
# entry costs nothing (the bot restores its labels once and then finds nothing to do). Deleting a
# line early is also safe: the bot's sweep restores any parked label whose owner is no longer
# under an active ban.
#
# Maintainer-only file (see CODEOWNERS), like the denylist it sits next to.

widecloud  2026-09-17  warn   # off-topic noise; first offence, penalty lifted 2026-09-18 — one life
